candidates.title: Inside the Circle (El círculo)
candidates.reason: Completed eight-episode Mexican political murder/conspiracy thriller, released October 7, 2026. Reporter Tomás's leaked footage of actress Pamela Dosantos's last sighting starts a dangerous inquiry into blackmail and powerful insiders. The full official episode guide supports an actual spread of evidence across the season: Jimena examines Pamela's video in episode 2; Tomás and Mario investigate a stylist/photographer in episode 4; Mario finds Pamela's intimate recordings in episode 5; fresh murders and Jimena's lead change the case in episode 6; Amelia confronts Carlos about Pamela and buried history in episode 7; and a new autopsy finding in episode 8 sends Tomás toward another mystery amid a kidnapping rescue. These are recurring leads and shifts, not proof of a continuous answer-per-scene cadence: investigation is substantial (7), but revelation_frequency and progressive_revelation are each a more cautious 6, separate from brisk overall pace (7). The main strengths are political conspiracy, corruption, deception, evidence leverage, sustained pursuit, suspense and investigative journalism. A Spanish-language full-season review describes steady momentum, deliberate information release and polished contemporary photography/editing, but warns that many characters, subplots and relationship conflicts sometimes crowd the mystery and strain the ensemble balance. The personal-friendship drama is therefore substantial (7), and not every escalation supplies a solved clue. The compromising video is treated as selective evidence leverage, not as a proven deepfake. Despite an important defense/security official, the story is political rather than a military-operations thriller. The grounded full-season account contains no organized rule-bound lethal game. Confidence is moderated because measurements come from published complete-season episode descriptions and critical reporting rather than direct viewing; avoid asserting disputed details from inconsistent third-party finale summaries.

research_rejections.reason: The six-part Netflix sea-creature thriller premieres October 8, 2026, but the currently consulted launch reviews and promotional material emphasize the creature/horror premise, not independently substantiated revelations distributed through all six episodes. Whole-season revelation cadence and all required DNA dimensions are not sufficiently established for a candidate today.

research_rejections.title: American Sweatshop
research_rejections.reason: A social-media moderator investigates a violent video, but whole-film synopsis and mixed critical/audience reactions indicate repeated dead ends, deterioration of the protagonist, and a late ambiguous encounter rather than a well-paced series of meaningful answers. Some reviewers find the script shallow or the payoff disappointing; this is investigation and psychological distress without sufficiently reliable progressive-revelation evidence for the current research candidate set.
